Commentary.Commentary: We are back! The players are back too as New Zealand players take their respective field positions. Zak Crawley and Alex Lees are the openers for England. Tim Southee to start with the ball for New Zealand. Here we go...
… Second Innings …

Now, it is time for England to bat. They need to put on a good show on a wicket which is a good one to bat on. New Zealand on the other hand, need to be patient and just hit the right lines and lengths. They will love a couple of wickets before Stumps.

The England bowlers were made to toil hard. The wicket had nothing on offer for them. However, they will be a tad disappointed with freedom they let New Zealand score at. They though bowled a lot better today. All of their bowlers except for Root got a wicket at least. Anderson was the pick with a three-fer.

What a sublime knock from Daryl Mitchell. He was the highlight and along with Blundell, the reason as to why the Kiwis are in such a strong position. Yes, there were others who got off to starts too but it was the massive 200-plus stand between those two which is what has turned the tide in the visitors’ favor. Mitchell was unlucky to not get a double ton. He kept losing partners and then was the last one to fall but a tremendous effort from him.
Finally the New Zealand innings comes to an end and we believe they have batted themselves into a very good position here. Probably in one from where they can’t lose the game.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Daryl Mitchell departs finally and with that the New Zealand's innings also comes to an end. A slower and wide delivery outside off, Daryl Mitchell reaches to cut it but gets a slight outside edge. The ball goes back to the keeper and Ben Foakes makes no mistake taking a good low catch. England players come up to congratulate Daryl Mitchell and everyone gives him a standing ovation. New Zealand are bowled out for 553!
Commentary.Howout: c Ben Foakes b Matthew Potts

Commentary.Commentary: Good running! A full delivery on off. Mitchell just pushes it towards the long on and comes back for the second run.
A fullish delivery, around off. Mitchell swings across the line but misses.
Broad continues his short-pitch stuff and angles this around leg. Boult ducks under it.
Back of a length angling into the body. Boult blocks it awkwardly towards the off side.
A short delivery around off. Boult lets it go.
A length delivery on off. Mitchell slogs it aerially towards long off. It falls in the vacant region and a single is taken.
We have a change of ball finally! The ball does not go through the gauge this time and England will finally get to replace this ball. Broad is ready with the new one and will steam in again.
Broad with a yorker, around off. Daryl Mitchell digs it out.
Angling into pads. Mitchell works it to fine leg but denies a single.

FOUR! Another boundary and New Zealand now reach 550! Another tossed up delivery on off. Almost a carbon copy of the last ball as Boult skips down the track and hammers it straight down the ground again. Boult is very happy with his shot and rightly so, these are crucial runs for New Zealand!
FOUR! This time he smashes it! A tossed up delivery on off. Boult charges down the track and slams it straight down the ground for a boundary.
This is outside off. Boult resist himself again and lets it go.
A flatter one on off. Boult blocks it out.
Tossed up, outside off. Trent Boult looks to go down the track but then decides to avoid the shot and puts his bat inside the crease.
Leach delivers this slower in the air and slightly shorter. Trent Boult goes back and mistimes his cut shot.
FOUR! Stuart Broad was trying for a yorker but ends up bowling a low full toss, Daryl Mitchell hits it hard and straight down the ground for a boundary. He moves to 187.
Brilliant fielding at deep square leg by Jonny Bairstow. Shorter and on middle, Daryl Mitchell pulls it hard towards deep square leg and Jonny Bairstow collects it diving to his right. No runs.
Fuller and outside off, Daryl Mitchell drives it through covers. Jack Leach gives it a long chase and gets it. They take a comfortable two.
Shorter and on middle, Daryl Mitchell pulls it again, this time towards the fielder at deep square leg.
Low full toss on middle, Daryl Mitchell flicks it towards the mid-wicket fielder.
FOUR! This is brilliant from Daryl Mitchell. He moves to 181 now. Shorter and on middle, Daryl Mitchell plays a pull shot through square leg for a boundary.
Wide outside off this time, left well alone by Trent Boult.
On off, defended.
Tossed up on middle with a hint of turn, Trent Boult defends it to point.

Trent Boult has done well to bring his foot back in time. Tossed up, outside off. Trent Boult gives the charge and looks to hit it away but misses. Foakes collects the ball quickly and whips the bails off. However, Boult brings his back leg inside the crease just in time as replays confirm it after the leg umpire takes it upstairs.
Outside off this time with a hint of turn, Trent Boult gets down the track but misses it. He is fast enough to get back in his crease.
FOUR! Tossed up on off, Trent Boult uses his feet and lofts it over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Goes fuller this time on middle, Daryl Mitchell blocks it away.
Shorter and on middle, Daryl Mitchell ducks under it.
Shorter and on leg, Daryl Mitchell looks to defend it but misses. Stuart Broad appeals but the finger stays down. Replay shows that the ball had hit his thigh.
FOUR! Shorter one again, Daryl Mitchell pulls it hard and through deep square leg for a boundary. This was well-timed fro Daryl Mitchell.
Shorter and on middle at 81 mph, Daryl Mitchell pulls it straight towards the fielder at deep square leg.
Back of a length and down the leg side, Daryl Mitchell flicks it to square leg.
On middle, this is defended to mid-wicket.
FOUR! Tossed up on middle, Trent Boult dances down the track and lofts it over mid-wicket for a one-bounce boundary. This was surprising from Trent Boult.
Full and on the middle, this is defended back towards the bowler.
Who will walk out now? Trent Boult is the new batter in.

OUT! CAUGHT! England get their ninth wicket and they have done well in this final session to keep New Zealand's score under control. Leach bowls that off stump line but it is not that fuller in length to drive off the front foot. However, Henry goes for it and does it aerially. He ends up hitting it straight to Zak Crawley at covers. He takes the catch comfortably and looks like New Zealand batters no longer want to hang in there and are going for everything now.
Commentary.Howout: c Zak Crawley b Jack Leach

Commentary.Commentary: Tossed up on off. Daryl Mitchell works it to long on for a single.
Short and outside off. Daryl Mitchell cuts it to deep point for a couple.
Matt Henry walks out to the middle now and Jack Leach is brought back into the attack.

OUT! CAUGHT! Back of a length and on leg, Tim Southee looks to block it awkwardly but fumbles and the ball hits the top part of his bat. It goes in the air and at gully where Root does no mistake. Two wickets in the over for Stuart Broad and England look much more confident now!
Commentary.Howout: c Joe Root b Stuart Broad

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and outside off, Tim Southee blocks it to the vacant silly point region.
FOUR! Tim Southee is off the mark straightaway with a boundary! Back of a length, around off. Southee rides the bounce and guides it through backward point for a boundary.
Who will walk out now? Tim Southee is the new batter in.

Broad has been going for his bouncers in this over and he bangs another one, it is around leg. Kyle Jamieson looks to hook it away. However, he gets a glove on it and Ben Foakes behind the stumps takes an easy catch moving to his left.
Commentary.Howout: c Ben Foakes b Stuart Broad

Broad starts the new spell with a shortish length, on the pads. Kyle Jamieson clips it to deep square leg for a single.
Stuart Broad comes into the attack.

On a length, outside off. Daryl Mitchell lets it go.

FOUR! James Anderson drifts on the pads this time. Kyle Jamieson just tucks it fine and the ball races away for a boundary. Runs have started to come quickly again after that wicket.

Potts bangs this short and down the leg side. Kyle Jamieson lets it go.

Potts comes 'rpund the wicket and serves a length ball around leg. Kyle Jamieson looks to defend but misses. The ball hits his pads and there is an appeal but the umpire says no. Pitching outside leg this, good decision by the umpire.

Another short delivery that is angling into leg. Kyle Jamieson ducks under it.
FOUR! 500 comes up for New Zealand! Potts tries a bouncer on middle. Kyle Jamieson goes for the pull and gets a huge top edge. The ball goes in the air and one bounce into the fence.
Back of a length, on off. Kyle Jamieson blocks it off the back foot.

Ohh...what a ball first up to face for Kyle Jamieson! Absolute cracker of a delivery this by James Anderson! He nails a inswinging yorker on middle. Kyle Jamieson does well to get his bat down in time and the ball goes off the inside half towards deep backward square leg for a single.
Kyle Jamieson is the next man in.

He tries to defend it but gets a thick outside edge and Joe Root at first slip takes a good low catch. A crucial breakthrough for England and this has been a brilliant little spell from James Anderson!
Commentary.Howout: c Joe Root b James Anderson

We are all ready for the final session! England players make their way out to the middle. The two New Zealand batters, Daryl Mitchell and Michael Bracewell are also back to resume their innings. Matthew Potts will continue his over. Here we go...
… DAY 2, SESSION 3 …

So, the post-Lunch session, a curtailed one, courtesy of a rain intervention, has been dominated completely by the Kiwis. Both Daryl Mitchell and Michael Bracewell were positive from the onset and New Zealand are now inching close to that 500 mark. England were pretty ordinary after Lunch as they leaked runs freely and especially Jack Leach turned out to be the favourite target of the New Zealand batters. It now looks like a matter of when New Zealand will declare rather than England getting all 10 wickets. However, England need to keep believing as it is a good batting track and has to make sure that they don't leak runs in the final session. Stay tuned for the post-Tea session...

UPDATE - 7.34 pm IST ( 2.04 pm GMT) - We have some good news folks! The rain has stopped and it has brighten up at the Trent Bridge. Also the news is that Tea will be taken early at 7.40 pm IST (2.10 pm GMT). The final session will begin at 8.00 pm IST (2.30 pm GMT).

UPDATE - 7.26 pm IST (1.56 pm GMT) - As our not so beloved friend, rain entertains us and stops the action on the field for sometime, this is a chance for England to regroup themselves. They have been poor post-Lunch and need to tighten things up as New Zealand are racing away towards that 500 mark and with rain coming now, they would be looking to keep going when we come back.

UPDATE - 7.06 pm IST (1.36 pm GMT) - Ohh...it has suddenly started raining out there! The players are running off the field and covers are coming on. Hopefully it is not a long delay and just a passing shower.

A fuller delivery on off. Mitchell defends it off the front foot.

We are all set for the afternoon session! England got a solitary wicket in the first session but it was a big one and just at the stroke of Lunch. Can they now cash in and bring that momentum into this session to restrict New Zealand to as low a total as possible. The England players make their way out to the middle and the Kiwi batters, Daryl Mitchell and Michael Bracewell are also ready to resume their innings. It promises to be a riveting session. Ben Stokes will start for England. Here we go...
… DAY 2, SESSION 2 …

England on the other hand, bowled a lot better than they did in the first session of Day 1. They only got the one wicket but they did not let the visitors score as freely as they did yesterday, It has been hard work for the bowlers as the wicket has not offered a lot. England need to continue to build pressure by bowling tidy lines and lengths. Do join us for the second session in a bit.

Another good session for the Kiwis and they now have a stronger hold on this game! Both Mitchell and Blundell continued from where they left off yesterday. Both got to their tons and added well over 200. Blundell fell shortly after he got to his ton but Mitchell along with Bracewell ensured there are no more wickets to fall before the break. New Zealand have crossed the 400-run mark and will now probably eyeing the 500-run mark which will bat them into a position from where their chances of losing the game becomes really low.

We are all set for Day 2, folks! The England players have made their way out to the middle. They have a new ball that is just seven overs old and they would like to make the most of it this morning. The two overnight Kiwi batters, Tom Blundell and Daryl Mitchell are marking their guard. It is Stuart Broad who will start the proceedings. Daryl Mitchell on strike. Here we go...

England on the other hand, will hope they can do something similar they did in the first game. Break this stand quickly and then run through the lower order. The second new ball is relatively new and you can’t rule the English bowlers out from doing so. They’ll be desperate to keep New Zealand under the 400-run mark. Do they have a hero in them?

New Zealand will surely be eyeing the 450-run mark at least. The pitch is a belter and it should be at its best on Day 2! Mitchell will be eyeing back-to-back tons whereas Blundell would want to get to his after missing out in the first Test. Can they do so is the question.

Yet another massive stand between Blundell and Mitchell has put their side in a commanding position. The question is, can they build on this now? The visitors failed to capitalise from a strong position in the first game but a slip up is not affordable here. The first session will be a very important one. Welcome to the coverage.
… DAY 2, SESSION 2 …

England on the other hand will be rueing the fact that they elected to bowl. The pitch has been a belter throughout and the England bowlers have been made to toil really hard. They really need a few early wickets on Day 2 if they are to get back in the game. They did do so in the first Test but can they do it again? We will find out. Do join us at 3:30 pm IST (10:00 am GMT).

England on the other hand, bowled with a lot more control in this session. They would know though another two wickets and they’ll be into the all-rounders. That is exactly what they’ll be looking for in the final session which promises to be another good one. Stay tuned.

England on the other hand, may just regret their decision of bowling first. It did seem like it was not the right one as their bowlers looked very ineffective. They though will be very pleased they got the two wickets towards the end of the session. However, they have conceded far too many runs than they would have liked and stemming the run-flow is what they will look to do after the break which might just result in wickets. Another exciting session awaits. Stay tuned.

For most of the part, it was New Zealand who ruled it! Their openers began brilliantly. The pitch was batting friendly and they made most of it. The two played in a positive manner and added 84. Both though fell in quick succession. Young missed out on a well-deserved half ton. Conway and Nicholls though have begun well and the visitors will hope there could be yet another big partnership.

A very fine and a very entertaining session of cricket! Have to say, both teams will be pleased with how things have gone. New Zealand probably would have loved to have lost a wicket less whereas, England would have liked to have conceded few more runs. Overall as a neutral, it was an action-packed two hours of cricket.

Matthew Potts comes into the attack.
On the off pole again, this is kept out.
On the off pole, Latham defends it solidly.
On off, Latham gets right behind the line and keeps it out.
Well outside off, Latham shoulders arms to this one. It was the tempter, Latham though evaded it.
On a length and on off, Latham pushes it to covers.
Young gets off the mark! Angled into the pads, it is worked towards square leg for on.
A harmless nut to end. Outside off, Latham does not fiddle with it.
Solid defensive stroke to this ball on off to end the over.
Three more! Just a mere push! Fuller and on off, this is hit down the ground, past mid off. He did not hit that way too hard and hence, it does not go to the fence. Three taken.
On the stumps, kept out.
On off, defended.
Outside off, left alone.
That was a close leave! After getting the last ball to move away, gets this one back in from just outside off. Latham leaves it alone. It goes just past the off pole.
BEATEN! Beauty! Length, angled into the off pole, lands and leaves the batter. Latham is beaten as he plays inside the line of the delivery.
On the stumps, kept out.
Angled into the pads, Latham works it to mid-wicket.
Closer to the off pole this time and defends it.
Tries to bowl the inswinger but the line is well outside off, left alone.
Angled into the pads, Young lets the ball come to him and then works it to mid-wicket.
Outside off, Young leaves it alone.

That has taken off! Really well played in the end by Young! This is on a length, it lands and gets big on the batter. Young does well to take one hand off the handle and defend it. He did that to keep the ball down. Really well played.
Angled into the off pole. Young keeps it out.
On off, defended well.
Makes the batter play, bowls it on the stumps, negotiated well by Young.
A lot of movment into the batter but the line was well outside off. Left alone.
On the off pole, blocked.

Another tight run but Young would have been in! On middle, this is worked to mid on. Broad runs in, picks it up with one hand and without gathering his balance has a shy at the bowler's end but misses.
Indecisive there! Another one just outside off, Young looks to play at it but then in the end, looks to leave it, it goes off the face and on the bounce to the slip fielder.
Nice and late! Doing what he was not doing in the last game, that is let the ball come to him. On a length and around off, Young plays it right under his eyes on the off side.
Good length and on off, defended.

FOUR! That is the shot of the morning so far! That is creamed. Off the front foot this time. After a short one, Broad goes full and on middle, Latham shows the full face of the bat and milks it down to the long on fence. Beautiful. So pleasing to the eye. End of a very good over for the kiwis.
FOUR! Solid punch! Slightly shorter in length and on off, Latham hangs back and pushes this through covers. Trademark Latham there. The outfield is really quick here.

Good half stop! Saves three for his side! Length and on off, Young looks to defend, this goes off the outside edge to the right of the fielder. He dives and gets a hand to it. It goes behind towards third man for one.
Tight run! Latham would have been in though! On off, this is pushed towards cover. Latham takes off. Stokes gets to the ball, turns and has a shy at the bowler's end but misses.
Outside off, a big grunt as Broad delivers the ball. Easy leave though for Latham.
Good length and on off, it is pushed to cover. Broad bowls this from around the wicket, like he usually does to left-handers.
A dot to end! On off, Young hangs back and blocks.
Now goes full, looks to target the pad of the batter, Young works it to square leg.

That is a beauty! Unplayable! Not a lot you can do with that but just hope it misses the outside edge! This is angled into the off and then Anderson gets it to leave the batter. Young is beaten as he tries to defend.
Good solid start by Young so far! Length and on off, this is pushed to covers.
Angled into the pads, Latham looks to flick but misses. It hits the pad and rolls on the leg side. A leg bye taken.
Starts this over with a length delivery outside off, Latham lets it through. Good pace in this surface but not a lot of movement so far.
Another harmless nut to end the over! Just the boundary from it then! The last ball is one outside off, not played at.
Solid! Length and around off, Young gets right behind the line and keeps it out.

FOUR! Off the mark in style! That should make Young feel a whole lot better. He has been short of runs lately but that is a good confident stroke. Shorter and around off, Young hangs back and pushes it through covers for a boundary.
Good length and on off, blocked.
Just outside off again, not played at.
Yes and no but alll safe in the end! Shorter and on off, Young looks to drop and run on the off side. He takes off but is sent back in time.
Stuart Broad to bowl from other end.
A maiden to begin with! A harmless nut to end. Outside off yet again, not played at. Not a lot of movement then in the first over for Anderson.
Just outside off again, left alone.
This one jags back in sharply! Length and outside off, it zips through and also comes back in. Hits Latham high on the pads.
Outside off, left alone.
Angled into the off pole, Latham solidly defends it.
Some swing to begin with! This one moves away, the line is well outside off. Left alone.

We are all set for the action to begin! The England players make their way out to the middle. They are followed by the New Zealand openers, Tom Latham and Will Young. James Anderson will bowl. Here we go...

Tom Latham says they wanted to bowl first too, there is a little bit of green tinge but seems dry. Adds they need to play the first hour well and it will get easier. Informs Kane is fine. Ends by saying they are playing 4 seamers and Nicholls comes in along with Bracewell.

Ben Stokes says the wicket tends to get better as the game goes on and they are looking to put them under pressure by taking wickets with the new ball. States they were going toe-to-toe in the last Test and he is very pleased with the guys for the effort and character they showed. Adds they just want to enjoy the game and do well. Informs Leach is fine and he was unfortunate in the last game.

NEW ZEALAND (PLAYING XI) - Tom Latham (C), Will Young, Devon Conway, Henry Nicholls (IN FOR Kane Williamson), Daryl Mitchell, Tom Blundell (WK), Michael Bracewell (IN FOR Colin de Grandhomme), Kyle Jamieson, Tim Southee, Matt Henry (IN FOR Ajaz Patel), Trent Boult.
ENGLAND (PLAYING XI) - Alex Lees, Zak Crawley, Ollie Pope, Joe Root, Jonny Bairstow, Ben Stokes (C), Ben Foakes (WK), Matthew Potts, Jack Leach, Stuart Broad, James Anderson.

New Zealand on the other hand, haven’t been at their best in this format this year. They have been pretty inconsistent. Can they turn it around though? They’ll have to do it without their best batter Williamson but they still have a lot of quality in their side. Toss coming up in a bit…
